findings.title: KeyError when existing Integration metadata has no `sender`
findings.body:
The new check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with no fallback. `sender` is only written when the Integration is created by the installation webhook (`state.get("sender")` in `build_integration`). Integrations created through the pipeline itself never get it; `test_basic_flow` asserts the metadata has no `sender` key. Integrations created before sender tracking also lack it.

Common case: an org uninstalls the GitHub integration in Sentry. The OrganizationIntegration is deleted but the Integration row stays. On reinstall, the code reaches this branch and raises an unhandled KeyError, so the user gets a 500 and cannot reinstall.

The lookup is also not filtered by `provider`, so a non-GitHub integration with a colliding `external_id` would fail the same way. Use `.get()` with a defined fallback (verify another way, or error cleanly), and filter by `provider="github"`.

findings.title: User/installation ownership check skipped when no Integration row exists
OAuth `state` is a static, predictable value (pipeline.signature)
findings.body:
`pipeline.signature` is an md5 of the pipeline view class names. It is the same for every user, org and session; the tests hard-code `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` across different users and orgs. Using it as the OAuth `state` gives no CSRF or code-injection protection: anyone can compute it, so a forged callback `?code=<attacker code>&state=<constant>` passes the check at line 412.

The PR description presents state validation as a security property, but it doesn't provide one. Generate a random nonce (for example `secrets.token_hex()`), store it in pipeline state, and compare it with `constant_time_compare`, as `OAuth2LoginView`/`OAuth2CallbackView` already do.

findings.title: Network/HTTP failures in token exchange or user lookup cause unhandled 500s
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` on line 423 sits outside the try block, so connection errors or timeouts propagate. `get_user_info()` calls `raise_for_status()` internally, so a 401 or 5xx from `api.github.com/user` (for example a revoked token or a GitHub outage) raises an uncaught HTTPError. In both cases the user sees a 500 instead of the integration-failed dialog. That dialog is what the opener window expects for its postMessage. Wrap these calls and return `error(...)` on failure.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the not-found path
findings.body:
The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`). The new state-mismatch check rejects it before the GitHub 404 is ever reached, and the assertion was changed to `"Invalid installation request."`.

As a result, the `build_integration` 404 path (`"The GitHub installation could not be found."`) is untested. The test name is also misleading. Use the correct state so the flow reaches the 404, and add a separate test for state mismatch.

There is also no test where an Integration exists with a matching `sender` and the install succeeds, and none where `sender` is missing (the KeyError case).

findings.title: Error strings no longer extractable for translation
findings.body: The old code wrapped literals directly, for example `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")`. The new helper calls `_(error_short)` on a variable, and callers pass plain string literals. `makemessages` only extracts literals passed to `_()`, so "Invalid installation request.", "GitHub installation pending deletion." and "Github installed on another Sentry organization." drop out of the translation catalogs. Wrap the literals at the call sites or in the default argument.
